name: Isaeus
bio: Isaeus was an Attic orator, counted among the canonical Ten Orators of Athens. Born about 420 BC, probably at Chalcis, he practised at Athens as a professional speech-writer, and by tradition he was a teacher of the young Demosthenes.

He specialised in cases of inheritance, wills and adoption, argued with a close, lawyerly skill. Eleven of his speeches survive whole, together with a large fragment of a twelfth. This archive carries them in Edward Seymour Forster's Loeb translation (1927).
